- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.77) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.30) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts often peak too early and then drop sharply, especially after sentiment spikes.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment upturns (e.g., sentiment >0.80) — model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model consistently misses downward trend turns after 10–15 days, especially when sentiment declines.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits recent highs and underweights sentiment decay — leads to false peaks.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high for 3+ consecutive days, model should not forecast 5–10% above recent high unless confirmed by price action.
- Avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection” — if sentiment drops sharply, model should not immediately reverse to extreme lows — allow 2–3 days of buffer before correction.
